process.quote: Any suspected breach of these Regulations must be referred to an Academic Conduct Officer of the Host School as soon as reasonably practicable.
process.anchor: Section B: 2. Notification of Breach and Initial Review

process.quote: The Academic Conduct Officer will consider the allegations made together with any evidence provided to them and, in understanding the scope of the case, may review any or all academic work previously submitted by the student during their current programme of study.
process.anchor: Section B: 2. Notification of Breach and Initial Review

process.quote: The student will be given the opportunity to make a statement and discuss the evidence they have submitted, as well as respond to the evidence presented by the Academic Conduct Officer.
The meeting will be attended by the student, the student's Companion (if any, as set out in B1), the Academic Conduct Officer, and a note-taker.

If a student fails to confirm their attendance or fails to attend the Academic Conduct Meeting without good reason, the Academic Conduct Officer will impose an outcome on the basis of the available evidence.

Students may be accompanied to an Academic Conduct Meeting or Academic Conduct Panel hearing by another Member of the University (usually either a member of staff or a fellow student who is independent from the case), or by an advisor from the Students' Union Advice Centre.
An appeal against a decision made by an Academic Conduct Panel may be made under the Regulations Governing Academic Appeals by Students.
The Academic Conduct Panel will be held as soon as reasonably practicable and normally within twenty (20) working days of the date of the notification being sent.
The outcome of an Academic Conduct investigation is decided on the basis of the evidence available and the balance of probabilities.
The University will record, monitor, and report academic conduct outcomes.

definitions.quote: Academic responsibility and conduct (previously known as academic integrity) is integral to studying at the University and a guiding principle of academic life.

Plagiarism: the use of ideas, intellectual property, or material derived from another source (including another student’s work, or content generated by any other person or computer software) without appropriate acknowledgement and/or indication, thereby presenting it as your own.
Cheating: any action before, during, or after an examination or assessment by which you seek to gain unfair advantage or assist another student to do so.
Collusion: working with another student or students in an unauthorised way to create academic work that should be created by a student independently.

This may include asking for unauthorised assistance with assessments, or engaging with essay mills, or using artificial intelligence tools in an unauthorised way to generate or alter the content or wording of academic work.
Falsification: any attempt to present fictitious or distorted data, evidence, references, experimental results, or other material and/or knowingly to make use of such material.

Recycling (sometimes referred to as ‘self-plagiarism’): where a piece of work that has already been submitted for assessment, is resubmitted, in whole or in part, for assessment in the same or in a different programme of study without appropriate acknowledgement and/or permission.
